trust_decision.summary: The property is that the path a path-scoped middleware is matched against must equal the path the Fastify router matched; the adapter's Nest-middleware wrapper derives it from the raw request target (fastify-adapter.ts:739-745) and the vendored middie engine derives it from req.url (fastify-middie.ts:114,189), so an absolute-form target ('GET http://host/users HTTP/1.1') routes to the controller but skips the middleware registered for /users.

landing_point.why: This is the only place the Fastify adapter turns a request target into the path used to decide whether Nest-registered middleware runs, so an engineer reading 'path-scoped middleware bypass via absolute-form request targets' starts at the forRoutes wrapper/sanitizeUrl pair here.

fix_sites.entry_point: new FastifyAdapter(options) - public adapter constructor used at application bootstrap
FastifyAdapter.use()/app.use(path, fn) (fastify-adapter.ts:775-783) and the same forRoutes registration; both end in fastify.use()
fix_sites.module_kind: vendored third-party plugin engine (deleted by the fix)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: That file is a vendored clone of the third-party @fastify/middie plugin (its own header says so, fastify-middie.ts:44-48), so request-target interpretation belongs to the plugin rather than to Nest - patching the adapter's sanitizeUrl, or waiting for an upstream release, looks like the whole fix.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Router options passed at the top level of the adapter options (caseSensitive:false, ignoreTrailingSlash, ignoreDuplicateSlashes, useSemicolonDelimiter) must keep normalising middleware paths; today the vendored engine reads both initialConfig.X and initialConfig.routerOptions, while @fastify/middie only reads routerOptions, so a fix that swaps in the upstream plugin (or rewrites the routerOptions merge) without folding the top-level keys breaks middleware matching for e.g. '//USERS/'.

O6_input_shapes: absolute-form with duplicate slashes and trailing slash '//USERS/' while ignoreDuplicateSlashes + ignoreTrailingSlash + caseSensitive:false apply
non-http(s) scheme and unparsable target left unchanged and left to the router (fix.diff:268-277)
query string is stripped from req.originalUrl before resolution (fastify-adapter.ts:739-744, then sanitizeUrl)

O8b_injection_room.sibling: resolve the request target before comparing the MiddlewareConsumer exclude list (it currently compares the raw httpAdapter.getRequestUrl result)
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: exclude matching has to agree with the router's path normalisation exactly like middleware matching does, and this is the generic core consumer of getRequestUrl, so a maintainer fixing the fastify bypass could have mirrored the same strip there.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: the same absolute-form strip for the 404 handler's registered-prefix skip (path = req.originalUrl.split(/[?#]/)[0])
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: the Express adapter uses the identical 'path <- req.originalUrl' idiom for a path decision, and a maintainer could plausibly have fixed both transports in one PR.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: resolve absolute-form inside getRequestOriginalUrl/getRequestUrl so every core consumer (middleware/utils.ts:128, not-found message) sees a path
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: it is the single producer feeding the core URL consumers, so it is the natural 'fix it once, deeper' alternative to patching sanitizeUrl in the middleware wrapper.
